description:
## Why this ticket exists

v0.2 turns spendbar from a run-on-demand CLI (v0.1, complete on branch `v0.1-ts-port`) into the service/view architecture: **`spendbar service run` is the headless daemon and SOLE snapshot writer**; menubar (v0.3) and MCP/CLI (T-013) are views/readers. The shape was fixed by four rounds of external Codex review of `product-architecture-2026-07-30.md` ("Service & data layer" + "Launcher + LaunchAgent" sections): round 2 forced minimal durable `install|start|stop` + launcher INTO v0.2 (a short-lived CLI/MCP invocation must hand indexing to something that survives its exit); round 3 added socket path rules and the honest headless definition; round 4 finalized stop/start sequencing. The zero-lifecycle-scripts rule (npm 12 / pnpm 10 block dependency scripts) is why the launcher design exists at all — nothing can be set up at install time.

## Scope — in

1. **`service run`**: headless daemon; acquires the writer lock using the primitive T-008 selected; single-instance guard (second instance exits cleanly, never publishes); hosts the refresh state machine; publishes only through T-010's generation/manifest protocol.
2. **Refresh state machine**: ONE execution queue; every job (fast tick, full, wake, manual, shutdown flush) carries a generation number; coalescing; **publish-if-current only**. This ticket builds the queue/state machine skeleton; T-012 plugs the two tiers into it.
3. **Control socket**: Unix-domain socket in a 0700 runtime dir; request IDs; bounded message sizes; timeouts; protocol version negotiation; operations = status / refresh / stop / progress. Credential model = whatever survived T-008 (peer-UID check, else fallback: 0700 dir + high-entropy 0600 auth token + constant-time compare). Socket path rules (round-3): short per-user path within macOS `sun_path` ≈104-byte limit (tested with long usernames/home paths); reject symlinked parent dirs; **probe a stale socket before unlinking** (a crash can leave a pathname no server owns).
4. **Launcher**: stable user-owned launcher at `~/Library/Application Support/spendbar/launcher` executing recorded absolute `[node, cli.js]` pairs from an allowlisted 0600 registry written only by spendbar. **NO PATH search** (attacker-controlled-binary risk; test with a poisoned PATH). Persistent **installation ID**; the launcher target changes only via explicit `install`/`repair` or a verified same-installation upgrade handoff. A foreground command from a different prefix/version **reports the mismatch** ("another installation owns the service — run `spendbar service repair` to adopt") and never silently retargets.
5. **Minimal durable `service install|start|stop`** + LaunchAgent plist targeting the launcher (no `LimitLoadToSessionType: Aqua` on the service — that key is menubar-view-only). **Stop sequencing (final, round-4)**: persist desired state = stopped → disable relaunch (KeepAlive would otherwise respawn) → request graceful shutdown OVER THE SOCKET → wait to deadline → then boot out the launchd job → remove only a verified-stale socket. Ordering matters: unloading first kills the process before it receives the request. `service start` reverses each step after partial failure. **No PID-based control anywhere** (PID reuse).
6. **`spendbar refresh`** CLI command (v0.2 phase deliverable): reader-side trigger over the socket; this is the "explicit user refresh" that bypasses T-012's full-tier cap.

## Scope — out

- Full upgrade/downgrade/prefix-change/nvm-removal matrix, `doctor`, `setup` wizard, uninstall ownership → v0.3. v0.3 adds the matrix, **not the mechanism** — the mechanism ships here.
- Menubar view and attach/quit semantics → v0.3.
- Zero-touch upgrade survival is explicitly NOT claimed: an npm upgrade/removal breaks the recorded path until the next foreground invocation of the OWNING installation re-validates + re-records, or the user runs `service repair`.
- Reboot persistence on SSH-only Macs with no GUI login: LaunchAgents load at user login, so no promise there; documented path is foreground `spendbar service run` (e.g. under tmux). "Headless" = no-menubar operation within a logged-in user session.
- Fast/full tier internals → T-012.

## State machines

- **Refresh queue**: queued → coalesced | running → publishing → published | discarded; generation numbers monotonic; publish-if-current is the only publish path.
- **Service lifecycle**: desired state (installed/started/stopped) vs actual; stop and start are multi-step sequences with per-step failure injection and reversal.
- **Lock ownership**: acquire → held (inode revalidation before EVERY publish and unlock) → released | lost; lease-losers discard results.

## Failure modes to test (each a named deterministic test)

- **Stale socket**: crashed server leaves an orphan pathname — probe classifies it dead before unlink; a live second server's socket is never unlinked.
- **Crashed service**: lockfile records pid + process-start-time + random owner token; PID-reuse simulated; lock file swapped under the holder is caught by inode revalidation.
- **Concurrent refresh races**: wake+timer, manual+full, midnight-crossing, shutdown flush, crash storms, wake storms — coalescing observed; no stale generation ever becomes current.
- **Partial stop/start**: failure injected at every stop/start transition; `start` recovers from any partial `stop`; a stopping service is not respawned by KeepAlive.
- **Two writers racing**: single-instance guard; loser discards, never publishes.
- **Foreign installation**: mismatch reported, registry unchanged.
- **Handoff** (v0.2 exit test): one short-lived CLI command starts indexing, exits; indexing completes with no foreground process — proven on a clean-prefix install.

## Dependencies on gate outcomes

- **T-008 (hard)**: implements whichever locking primitive survived (audited pure-JS package vs own lockfile with inode revalidation) and the prototyped socket credential design + validated socket path rules. Do not write lock or socket-auth code before T-008's verdict is recorded.
- **T-010 (hard)**: the state machine publishes exclusively through T-010's durability ordering (write gen → fsync gen → manifest temp → rename → fsync dir); publish-if-current composes with manifest replacement; schema-range policy means an older writer refuses to publish on a newer schema.
- T-009 is not a dependency of this ticket (MCP-side only).

## Constraints

No npm lifecycle scripts; no native builds; `usage.py` is frozen and never modified (service is TS-only); `package.json` never carries an author field; no real transcript data or personal paths in fixtures — service tests run on synthetic corpora.

## Approach notes

Design the state machine around an injectable clock/scheduler from day one or the race tests will be flaky; the plan's quality bar requires deterministic tests, not sleeps. Launchd plist load behavior needs a macOS runner (CI section of the plan) and some paths may only be verifiable via abstraction plus owner-machine runs — record which is which.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Clean-prefix install test: `service install` + `service start`, then one short-lived CLI command triggers indexing and exits; a new generation is published with no foreground spendbar process remaining (the v0.2 handoff exit test).
2. Control socket round-trips status/refresh/stop/progress with request IDs; oversized messages rejected; unauthenticated peer rejected per the T-008 credential design; protocol-version mismatch returns a typed error.
3. Socket path tests: a naive path exceeding ~104 bytes (long username/home) yields a compliant path or a clear error; symlinked parent dir rejected; stale-socket probe unlinks only verified-dead sockets and never a live server's socket.
4. Stop sequencing: failure injected at each step (persist desired state, disable relaunch, socket shutdown, deadline wait, bootout, socket removal); after any partial failure `service start` restores a working service; a stopped service does not respawn via KeepAlive.
5. Single-instance guard: a second `service run` exits with a clear message and never publishes; lease-loser discard verified via inode revalidation test (lockfile replaced under holder → publish refused).
6. Deterministic race tests pass without sleeps-as-synchronization: wake+timer, manual+full, midnight-crossing, shutdown flush, crash storm, wake storm; publish-if-current holds in every schedule (no superseded generation becomes current).
7. Launcher: registry file mode 0600 in 0700 dir; launcher refuses targets not in the allowlisted registry; runs correctly with a poisoned PATH containing a fake `node` (proving no PATH search); foreign-prefix invocation prints the repair-to-adopt mismatch message and changes nothing.
8. No PID-based control: control flows only via socket + lockfile owner token; a codebase search for kill-by-pid control paths comes up empty.
9. `spendbar refresh` reaches the running service over the socket and triggers a refresh; with no service running it fails with a clear, typed message.

## Risks
T-008 is a release gate that can invalidate both the lock and socket-auth designs — it is scheduled day-1 so failure re-plans early, but this ticket must not start those two components before the gate verdict. Launchd behavior is only partially testable in CI (macOS runner required; some sequences may need owner-machine verification — record which). Race tests become flaky unless the scheduler/clock is injectable from the first commit. The launcher registry is security-sensitive (0600 allowlist, no PATH search); a shortcut here becomes an attacker-controlled-binary execution path.

## Open questions (owner decisions)
1. Exact runtime-dir location for the socket: the plan mandates a 'short per-user runtime path' under the ~104-byte sun_path limit but names no path ($TMPDIR-derived vs ~/Library/... trade-off).
2. Wire framing for the control protocol: the plan fixes properties (request IDs, bounded sizes, version negotiation) but not the encoding (JSON-lines vs length-prefixed).
3. Mechanism for 'disable relaunch' in the stop sequence (plist rewrite of KeepAlive vs launchctl override) and the exact plist keys (RunAtLoad, ThrottleInterval, KeepAlive shape).
4. Whether a minimal `service repair` (adopt) ships in v0.2 — the mandated mismatch message references it, but the phase table lists only install/start/stop as the v0.2 minimum.
5. Graceful-shutdown deadline value before bootout (no number in the plan).
title: Headless service: run/install/start/stop, launcher, control socket, refresh state machine
